bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the National Minimum Wage and Annual Pay

If you have ever asked yourself **what is minimum wage in australia**, you are not alone. Many workers and job seekers want to know the baseline hourly rate and how it translates into annual, fortnightly, or weekly pay. This article explains the conversion, the role of tax and super, and the difference between the National Minimum Wage, award rates, and casual loading.

### The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026

The Fair Work Commission sets the National Minimum Wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the rate is **$26.44 per hour** for a full-time employee working 38 hours per week. That works out to **$1,004.90 per week** before any deductions. For casual employees, the rate includes a 25% casual loading, bringing it to **$33.05 per hour**. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave and other entitlements.

It is important to note that many employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that may set a higher minimum rate. The National Minimum Wage is the floor; your actual pay could be higher. Check the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data) for industry-specific rates.

### Converting Hourly to Annual Pay

The basic formula for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a standard 38-hour week, this becomes:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For the National Minimum Wage of $26.44:

$26.44 × 38 × 52 = **$52,271.44** (rounded)

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is a straightforward estimate. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the formula accordingly. For example, a part-time employee working 20 hours per week at $30 per hour would earn $30 × 20 × 52 = $31,200 annually.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply double the weekly figure. For the minimum wage:

- Weekly: $1,004.90
- Fortnightly: $2,009.80

Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing job offers. You can use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

### Tax on Your Annual Pay

Once you have your annual gross, you need to estimate tax. The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) provides the resident tax rates for 2026–27:

- Nil tax on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Additionally, most residents pay the **Medicare levy** of 2% of taxable income (with reductions for low-income earners). For a single person earning $52,271 (the minimum wage annual figure), the tax calculation is:

- Tax on $18,200–$45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$52,271: ($52,271 – $45,000) × 30% = $2,181.30
- Total tax: $4,020 + $2,181.30 = **$6,201.30**
- Medicare levy: $52,271 × 2% = **$1,045.42**
- Total tax and Medicare: **$7,246.72**

This leaves an estimated take-home pay of about **$45,024.72** per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for a more personalised estimate.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation (super) into a fund on your behalf. The super guarantee rate is **12% of your ordinary earnings** (the base hourly rate times hours worked). This is paid on top of your salary, not deducted from it. For the minimum wage:

- Super: $52,271 × 12% = **$6,272.53** per year

However, super is only paid on earnings up to the maximum contribution base of **$270,830** per year. For most minimum wage workers, this cap does not apply. Super is an important part of your total compensation package. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Distinguishing Award Rates and Casual Loading

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum, but many industries have modern awards that set higher rates. For example, hospitality or retail awards often have specific minimums for different classifications. Always check your award or agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides resources to find your correct rate.

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate. This loading is meant to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave, annual leave, or public holidays. When using a calculator, never enter a rate that already includes casual loading; instead, enter the base rate and select the casual loading option if applicable. Our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains this further.

### Average Weekly Earnings for Context

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes Average Weekly Earnings (AWE). As of May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were **$2,083.70 per week**. All employees total earnings (including part-time) averaged **$1,579.20 per week**. These figures are averages, not medians for a specific job. They give a sense of the broader labour market.

### Important Disclaimer

This article provides estimates only. Annual pay is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a more accurate picture, use [the timesheet](/) to enter your own hours and rate, and consult a tax professional or the ATO for your individual circumstances.

### Summary

Knowing **what is minimum wage in australia** is the first step to understanding your earning potential. The National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour translates to about $52,271 annually for a 38-hour week. After tax and Medicare, take-home pay is around $45,025, plus super of $6,273 paid into your fund. Whether you are comparing a salary offer or planning your budget, the formula hourly × 38 × 52 gives a quick annual figure. Remember to check award rates and consider casual loading if applicable.
